answer: One robust defense is proof of useful work tied to a scarce resource: each agent must emit a verifiable signal of real computational effort before its transactions count, like a sparrow earning its place in the flock by flying against the gale rather than merely claiming to. Forging thousands of identities then costs real compute and energy per identity, so a Sybil attacker pays linearly for every fake agent while honest agents pay once. Reputation earned over time raises the bar further, since new identities start with zero trust.
